facts.text: A requirement is a written statement of what a system must do, precise enough to be tested; requirements-based testing means every test checks a named requirement and every requirement has at least one test.
facts.quote: A requirement is a written statement of what the system must do, precise enough to be tested, and requirements-based testing means that every test exists to check a named requirement and every requirement has at least one test.

facts.text: A good engineering requirement states one thing under stated conditions, includes a measurable quantity, and carries an identifier.
facts.quote: A good engineering requirement states one thing, under stated conditions, with a measurable quantity, and carries an identifier.

facts.text: ISO 19014-4, the off-road software standard, requires systematic development.
facts.quote: The off-road software standard ISO 19014-4 requires systematic development

facts.text: The 2020 edition of ISO 19014-4 has an annex on software validation test environments covering simulation, hardware-in-the-loop and the machine.
facts.quote: its 2020 edition has an annex on software validation test environments: simulation, hardware-in-the-loop and the machine [Chapter 13].

facts.text: Requirements-based software assurance, including formal and static verification, is among the booklet's approaches and finds logic errors, interface violations and traceability gaps without field exposure.
facts.quote: The booklet counts requirements-based software assurance, with formal and static verification, among its approaches: it finds logic errors, interface violations and traceability gaps without field exposure

facts.text: Requirements-based software assurance with formal and static verification cannot prove that a learned perception model recognizes real scenes.
facts.quote: but cannot prove that a learned perception model recognizes real scenes [Chapter 1].

facts.text: Evidence that would satisfy the functional safety engineer includes requirements-to-test traceability and a map showing which test environment is used for each requirement.
facts.quote: What would satisfy the functional safety engineer includes requirements-to-test traceability and a map showing which test environment is used for which requirement [Chapter 13].

facts.text: The booklet recommends freezing a machine-readable hierarchy of requirements, hazards and scenarios early.
facts.quote: The booklet recommends freezing a machine-readable hierarchy of requirements, hazards and scenarios early [Chapter 9]

facts.text: The booklet suspects that requirements definition, rather than test count, was the real bottleneck in past programs.
facts.quote: suspects that requirements definition rather than test count was the real bottleneck in past programs

facts.text: The booklet lists a requirements debate consuming the four months as a program failure mode.
facts.quote: lists a requirements debate consuming the four months as a failure mode [Chapter 13].

facts.text: Braking requirements must come from the new hazard analysis, not from a criterion of being equal to or better than the old warning system.
facts.quote: The braking requirements must come from the new hazard analysis, not from "equal to or better than the old warning system" [Chapter 13].

facts.text: Requirements determine what the simulator must prove; without requirements, the number of scenarios run represents activity rather than evidence.
facts.quote: Requirements decide what the simulator must prove. Without them, "number of scenarios run" is activity, not evidence.
